name: tffr-dropring
metrics: latency 13 gt, reset 6 gt, min-pulse 1 gt
caption: T flip-flop with reset, 8 blocks (track memory): the dropper-ring T flip-flop (two droppers, two hoppers between them, a comparator reading dropper B) with a reset input next to dropper B only. name: dff-window
metrics: latency 4 gt, edge falling, setup 0 gt, hold 2 gt
caption: D flip-flop (falling edge), 10 blocks, redstone only (track memory): repeater M copies d into q only during a short window after the clock's falling edge. Its lock C (a comparator) reads a dust A that the clock powers while on and that a stone powers while off (through a subtract comparator with a redstone block behind it: NOT clock); the stone comes back 2 gt after the falling edge, so C drops for one short window and M takes d.

name: dffe-window
metrics: latency 4 gt, edge falling
caption: D flip-flop with enable (falling edge), 13 blocks, redstone only (track memory): the window D flip-flop (repeater M copies d into q during a short window after the clock's falling edge, its lock C reads a dust A powered by the clock while on and by a NOT-clock stone while off) plus a second subtract comparator with a redstone block behind it that powers A while e is off (NOT e): with e off the lock never drops and M keeps q.

name: shift2-window
metrics: N 2, latency 4 gt, edge falling
caption: Shift register of 2 cells (falling edge), 20 blocks, redstone only (track memory): two repeater latches in a row, M1 (d in) then M2 (q out), opened by one window wire A that the clock powers while on and a NOT-clock stone S (subtract comparator + a delay-3 repeater) powers while off, so A is off for 5 gt after the falling edge. M2's lock is a comparator on A: M2 is open 2..7 gt after the fall and copies M1's old bit. M1's lock is a delay-4 repeater on A: M1 is open 4..9 gt after the fall, and its own delay-4 repeater lets the new bit out at 8 gt, after M2 has locked.

name: counter19-items
metrics: N 19, output toggles every 19 pulses
caption: Item counter, 19 items, 39 blocks (track memory, `mctas circuit memory items --n 19`): the one counter whose size does not depend on N. Droppers A and B face each other and hold 19 items between them; each pulse fires exactly one of them, so the pile walks from A to B and back and each dropper runs empty once every 19 pulses. Comparators a and b read them (level 0 only when empty), so the wall torches on their output blocks are lit exactly when their own dropper is empty, and both torches power the copper bulb W above them: W toggles once every 19 pulses and is the output. W is also the phase. Comparator C reads it and its dust line powers the stone south of A, which holds A; the wall torch on that stone is lit only when the line is off, and its line holds B through the stone east of it. A held dropper is one kept continuously powered: it sees no rising edge, so a pulse fires only the other one. The pulse is the dust on the two lids, since a dropper fires on a signal at its own cell or at the cell above it.

Comparator C reads X's level L into dust A, and K2 (compare, redstone block beside it) gives 15 only at L = 15. Z subtracts K2's signal (through repeater F, 8 gt) from A (through repeater R1, 2 gt), and repeater W squares it: S = (0 < L < 15). Because the full signal arrives 6 gt late, a box that is filled to 14 at once and topped up a gt later still makes S rise. V subtracts S (through repeater f) from S delayed (T2) and pulses for 4 gt when S falls: when a loading box gets full, or when an unloading box gets empty. P fires from V directly. name: mono-nonretrig-2stage-k1
metrics: L 118 gt, delay 20 gt, retrigger non-retriggerable, re-arm 160 gt, min-pulse 1 gt
caption: Two comparator rings (crates/circuit-timer/src/long.rs). Stage 1 (two comparators, round 4 gt): a rising edge charges stage 1 through a gate (copper bulb, comparator K, observer O1, a delay-3 repeater, a subtract comparator into I1 whose side a repeater feeds from the dust between stage 1's stone A1 and stage 2's stone A2: every edge is ignored until the output itself has ended); stage 2 sits north of stage 1, fed through a repeater, a dust line and a second repeater; once its charge stops it decays 2 per round, so its output lasts at least 28 gt. A repeater reading its stone A1 powers stage 2's stone I2: stage 2 is a ring of 3 comparators (round 6 gt) that loses 1 per round, refilled evenly at 15 by stage 1's long output; once stage 1 dies it counts its levels down, and the output lamp beside its stone A2 goes dark at 0.
